Customize your Appearance with Vanity Items!


Cosmetic Vanity items help you create your unique look tailored to your class fantasy.

You can find a huge selection on the Auction House! Click the Rarity Dropdown and select Vanity. Then hit Search!

You can Ctrl + Left Click an item to preview its appearance. Find and Buyout any Vanity item on the Auction House.

Max level builds are significantly more powerful than leveling builds. It's vital that you upgrade your build at max level to succeed in end-game content.

• You can find many end-game ready builds in the Hero Architect. Hit N, then click the Hero Architect Tab, then select either Level 60 or 70 Builds depending on your current level.

{T:Interface\Tutorials\PathToAscension\endgamebuilds1:2:1}

You can scroll through high-rated end game builds to find one that matches your playstyle!

End-game builds rely on Mystic Enchants. Each build will show the required Mystic Enchants at the bottom of the build page.

{T:Interface\Tutorials\PathToAscension\endgamebuilds2:2:1}

You should acquire the Legendary and Epic enchants suggested immediately to unlock the full power of the build, then seek out the Blue and Green enchants as soon as possible.

• It is highly recommended you try out featured builds before trying to create your own end-game build. You can also reference high-rated builds when creating your own to start with a strong foundation.

Once you choose a build and begin to grow comfortable with it, don't be afraid to experiment and adjust the build to your specific style of play.

{T:Interface\Tutorials\PtA\10_1:1024:406:1024:512:0:1024:59:465}

Item Level Shows Your Gear Power!!


The first step to improving your power at end-game is to improve your gear. It's time to start replacing your leveling gear with max level gear!

Mouse over any piece of gear to see the item level. This is a good general measurement of gear's power.

You can view your Average Item Level in your character sheet. This is an approximation of how strong your gear is!

Upgrade Gear - Increase Your Item Level!


There are many paths to upgrading your gear:
•Complete Dungeons
•Quest in Max Level Zones
•Enter the Manastorm

Extract 3 Epic Enchants to your Enchant Collection


Epic Mystic Enchants can be found by Reforging, the Auction House, and exploring the world. Epic Enchants offer huge leaps in power!

Try to collect 3 Epic Enchants that directly empower your current spells or Archetype.

If you run out of Mystic Extracts you can Reforge until you get more!

Craft and Gather Useful Items with Professions!

Professions help you level! Using your profession grants experience while also providing gear, consumables, and materials. You can start by learning two primary professions, and all the secondary ones!

•Primary Gathering Professions: Gatherers can pick up crafting materials around the world. They can sell them for gold, or use the items in their crafting professions.

•Primary Crafting Professions: Crafters can make equipment and other useful items from materials found by gathering professions.

•Secondary Professions: These life skills can be used by anyone without restriction!

{page} {T:Interface\Tutorials\PtA\78_2:1024:406:1024:512:0:1024:59:465}

Learn a Profession!


Visit a Beginner’s Book of Artisans to learn your first Profession. Find one using the Map Lens! You can unlearn a profession at any time to learn a new one.

Try to pick two primary professions that work well together like Skinning and Leatherworking, or Herbalism and Alchemy! This way you can gather your own materials to skill up without having to rely on other players.

{page} {T:Interface\Tutorials\PtA\78_3:1024:406:1024:512:0:1024:59:465}

Skill Up Your Profession!

You can level up your profession just by using it! Use the Skills Tab (Hotkey K) to view your current, and skill level. Visit a Profession Trainer to increase your maximum skill as you progress.

Difficulty colors guide you on what to do next to skill up. Always try to aim for orange level skills!

•Orange: Always grants a skill point!
•Yellow: Usually grants a skill point.
•Green: Rarely grants a skill point.
•Grey: Does not increase your skill.
•Red: Your skill level isn’t high enough yet!

{page} {T:Interface\Tutorials\PtA\78_4:1024:406:1024:512:0:1024:59:465}

As you craft and gather using your professions, you’ll rank up!

New recipes become available as you gain skill and you can train them at Profession Trainers or the Book of Artisans. Other recipes can be found throughout the world as loot or purchased from vendors and the auction house.

If you want to learn more than two Primary Professions, use a Craftsman’s Codex to gain an additional primary profession slot! You can buy them from Nozdormu, the Auction House, or the webstore.

Mystic Enchants are separated by quality; Rare, Epic, Legendary, and Artifact. These enchants will enhance spells, change abilities, or improve stats in different ways.

•Rare Enchants - Offers notable ability improvements or stat boosts. You can have active up to 6 Rare enchants at once.

•Epic Enchants - Moderately impoves abilities and stats. Your character is limited to 3 active Epic enchantments.

•Legendary Enchants - Capable of completely transforming spell and ability mechanics. Only one Legendary enchant can be used per specialization.

•Artifact Enchant- Teaches you a new and powerful spell or ability.

You can activates a total of 11 Mystic Enchants in a single specialization; 6 Rare, 3 Epic, 1 Legendary, and 1 Artifact.

Fill every active slot with an enchantment of the appropriate quality.

You can utilize the search bar in the Enchant Collection tab of the Mystic Enchants UI to filter by spells and abilities that you currently possess and find enchants that offer improvements to them. Choosing the Path of Finesse makes Agility your main stat, enhancing your offensive potential. You gain bonus Agility, and each point further increases your Attack Power, Critical Strike Chance, and Critical Strike Damage, sharpening every strike you land.

The Path of Finesse also provides two powerful passive abilities based on your weapon setup:

Agile Strikes: When wielding a one-handed weapon, your damaging melee and ranged abilities have their global cooldown and energy/mana cost reduced by 8%, allowing for faster, more efficient combat flow.

Fatal Wounds: When using a two-handed weapon, your melee and ranged ability critical strike damage bonus is increased by 20%, turning every critical hit into a devastating blow.

Agility is the Primary Attribute for those who rely on speed, precision, and deadly efficiency. It’s ideal for players who prefer fast-paced combat, weaving together rapid attacks, critical strikes, and nimble movement.

Alchemy is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession for players who want to create powerful consumables that enhance combat performance, provide utility, and support group content. To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn alchemy. Once you've trained the skill, you can start collecting the materials needed to craft your Recipes. Alchemy relies primarily on herbs gathered through Herbalism, though some potions may also require items purchased from Vendors or obtained in the world.

Using crafted potions is as simple as clicking on them in your inventory, but creating them can require access to an alchemy lab. While lower-level potions can be crafted anywhere, some advanced recipes may require special crafting areas, depending on the level of difficulty.

Alchemy does not require a tool for most crafts, but a philosopher’s stone can be needed for some transmutations. Ameer Greatluck is a helpful NPC located in all Capital Cities who provides access to the Recovery Services menu which can restore accidentally lost items. Area: 52 is Ascension’s main Classless Realm, where players build their heroes by choosing spells and Talents from any of the original vanilla classes. This system offers deep customization and endless build variety, allowing you to craft truly unique playstyles.

Sub-Zones are smaller, named areas within a larger zone. The first time you enter a Sub-Zone, you’ll earn a small amount of Experience and unveil its unique location on your World Map, helping you track where you’ve been.

You can hover your mouse over any revealed area on the World Map to see the name of the Sub-Zone. These areas are often tied to quests, gathering materials, and exploration achievements, making them valuable to discover during your journey.

Arena Rating is a score that reflects your performance and skill level in rated Arena matches. 

Every player begins at a base rating of 0, and your score will increase or decrease depending on the outcome of your matches. Winning a match raises your rating, while losing one reduces it. This system ensures you're paired against opponents of similar skill, making for more balanced and competitive fights.

Each Arena bracket (1v1, 2v2, and 3v3) has its own separate scoring, meaning your performance in one bracket won’t affect your rating in the others. This allows players to specialize in their favorite formats without penalty.

The Arena Season is a defined competitive period during which players participate in rated Arena matches to climb the Arena Rating ladder. Each season offers a fresh opportunity to compete for exclusive seasonal rewards.

With the start of every season, a new tier of PvP equipment becomes available for purchase from the PvP Quartermaster, using Arena Points. While some of this gear is accessible to all players, the most powerful equipment requires you to achieve a specific Arena Rating before they can be unlocked for purchase.

At the end of the season, ratings reset, rankings are tallied, and top-performing players receive special end-of-season rewards. Once a new season begins, all players start fresh, ready to compete again in a new cycle of progression and prestige.

You can view the current, previous, and upcoming seasons at:

Armor Type determines the kind of gear your character can equip and how much physical protection it provides. There are four types of equipment: Cloth, Leather, Mail, and Plate.

Different armors offer different levels of Armor rating, which reduces incoming physical damage.

- Cloth offers the least protection but is commonly used by casters for its magical bonuses.
- Leather provides moderate defense and is favored by agile classes.
- Mail offers more hardiness but still some dexterity and is used by archers or armored casters.
- Plate delivers the highest physical resistance and is worn by a melee fighter or a Tank.

The type of equipment you can wear is determined by your class, and you may need to train your proficiencies at a Class Trainer to wear higher-tier types like Mail or Plate.

Choosing the right equipment isn’t just about defense. Each piece of gear often comes with stats tailored for specific roles, like Intellect for casters or Strength for melee builds. Wearing the proper equipment for your role ensures both survivability and performance in combat.

Armor is a defensive stat that reduces the physical damage your character receives. It is found on most pieces of gear, and its value is heavily influenced by the item’s Armor Type (such as cloth, leather, mail, or plate).

The higher your armor rating, the less damage you take from physical attacks, making it a key stat for survivability in both PvE and PvP.

You can view your current Armor value in Character Info (Hotkey C).

Bags expand your inventory space by increasing the number of item slots your character can carry. Every character begins with a permanent 16-slot backpack and has four additional bag slots where larger or specialized bags can be equipped to hold even more items.

Bags come in a variety of sizes and types, and can be purchased from vendors, found on the Auction House, looted from enemies, or bought from the Ascension Store. Some bags function as containers for specific items only, like gathering or crafting materials, and cannot hold other objects.

Bloodforged equipment is Soulbound PvE gear that has been transformed into Bind-on-Equip PvP gear. This process allows previously Soulbound items to become tradable.

The Guild Bank is a large shared storage space available to members of a Guild. It allows players to store and share items, materials, and gold within their community, making it easier to manage resources collectively.

You can access the Guild Bank at special NPCs located in major cities. Guild leaders have control over permissions, deciding which members can deposit or withdraw items and funds to maintain organization and security.

As the Guild grows, additional storage tabs can be purchased to expand the Guild Bank. This extra space helps support group activities like raiding, crafting, and other events, by providing plenty of room for important items.

Unlike the Realm-Wide Bank, the Personal Bank is character-specific and can only be accessed by the character who owns it. It can be summoned only in rested areas, such as in an Inn or a Capital City, or in Raid instances.

If you still need more room, consider purchasing a Personal Bank or a Realm-Wide Bank from the Auction House for in-game currency, or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Base Health is the foundational amount of health points (HP) your character has before any modifiers from equipment, Talents, buffs, or enchants are applied. It represents your character’s unmodified durability, determined by your class and level.

This value is important because many abilities, scaling effects, and mechanics (especially those related to healing, tanking, or health-based damage) calculate their effects as a percentage of base health, not your total HP after bonuses.

For example, if a talent or spell states that it heals for “5% of Base Health,” it will always refer to that unmodified amount, ensuring consistent scaling regardless of your gear or buffs.

A character’s base health is the starting amount of health points before any talents, buffs, or equipment are applied. \r\n\r\nThis represents your character’s unmodified health pool, which many abilities and mechanics use as a reference for mana costs or scaling effects.

Base Mana is the default amount of mana a character has before any bonuses from gear, Talents, buffs, or enchantments are applied. It represents your character’s unmodified mana pool, which many abilities and mechanics use as a reference for mana costs or scaling.

This value is important because many abilities, scaling effects, and mechanics (especially those related to spellcasting) calculate their effects as a percentage of base mana, not your total mana pool after bonuses.

Donation Points (DP) are a premium currency used in the Ascension Store to purchase cosmetics, Heirlooms, Bags, Companions, and a wide range of convenience items. DP allows players to support the development of the server while unlocking useful features and stylish gear.

While your DP balance is shared across your entire account, different realms may use different currencies. Live realms use DP, while PTR or testing realms (such as Conquest of Azeroth during its testing phase) use RDP.

RDP functions like DP but is exclusive to PTR realms. When a PTR realm graduates to a live realm, it resets its economy, and all future purchases must be made with standard DP.

Most items purchased with these points are tradable and can be found on the Auction House or exchanged with Tiraxis for in-game currency, giving even non-donating players a way to access premium content.

You can access the store through the Ascension launcher or at ascension.gg/store.

You can buy a Book of Ascension from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency. Alternatively, you can purchase one from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

The Book of Artisans is a convenient, summonable companion pet that functions as a portable Profession Trainer. When summoned, it allows your character to learn any Profession or trainer-taught Recipe, just as if you were speaking to a trainer in a capital city or quest hub.

This tool is especially valuable for players leveling professions across multiple characters or frequently changing Profession setups. With the Book of Artisans, there’s no need to travel across the world to visit individual trainers.

You can buy a Book of Artisans from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency. Alternatively, you can purchase one from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

The Book of Artisans is one of the companions saved in your Vanity Collection, making it available to all your characters on the same realm once unlocked.
The Book of Artisans is a Profession Trainer in the form of a summonable Companion that can teach your character any Profession or Recipe that’s available from other Profession Trainers.

Archetypes are pre-constructed builds engineered to give newcomers a structured introduction to Ascension's classless system.

When you are creating your character, click archetype and you’ll be prompted to choose a role and playstyle. Once you do, you’ll see epic classless builds pulled from the Hero Architect based on your choices. 

Pick one, and you’ll enter the world as that archetype with everything you need to start playing. 

As you play, you’ll automatically learn your archetype’s spells, talents, and mystic enchantments, so you can take on greater challenges recommended if you're new to Ascension or to Azeroth as a whole, these character builds will help introduce you to Ascension game mechanics and the world of Azeroth while you imagine your ultimate hero.  

If you ever want to opt-out of your archetype while you are playing, visit Stony Tark and turn off the Build-Draft Game Mode.

Archetypes are pre-built classless builds designed to help newcomers get started by automatically granting spells, talents, and enchantments as you play. Chosen in character creation, they offer structured introductions to Ascension’s mechanics, and can be disabled anytime by visiting Stony Tark.

The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is your central interface for customizing and managing your character build on Ascension classless realms. In Wildcard Mode, this menu lets you review your current spells and Talents, reroll unwanted rolls with Scrolls of Fortune, browse possible abilities, and plan stronger combinations. It also includes Skill Cards, where you can view your account-wide collection and activate cards during the early levels of a build. You can save and manage Specializations to switch between different builds, and each Specialization has its own build setup so you can experiment without overwriting your other specs.

Call Board Daily Quests offer a wide selection of objectives spanning PvE, PvP, world content, professions, and more. Available through the Call Board in each Capital City, these quests are a key source of end-game rewards and daily progression. Completing Call Board dailies can earn Marks of Ascension, Honor Points, Call Board Caches, and other catch-up rewards. The Call Board stores up to 7 days worth of quests, refreshing with new objectives every day. This system gives you flexibility to log in on your own schedule without missing out. If you fall behind or are short on time, you can auto-complete missed dailies using gold or Bazaar Tokens.

These caches are reward chests earned by completing the Call Board Daily Quest. Designed as a catch-up mechanic, these caches are ideal for helping players quickly gear up for current content, especially if you're returning to the game or leveling a fresh character.

Each cache has a high chance to contain gear upgrades, from Dungeon gear to epic Raid loot from all previously released content, scaling up to the most recently released Raid. If you receive a cache from a daily quest requiring PvP activities, the gear from your cache will be Bloodforged.

These chests offer a reliable alternative to repetitive farming, giving you access to relevant power gains even if you're behind the current progression curve. They're especially helpful for preparing alts or off-specs for group content.

The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is the central hub for customizing your character. This menu allows you to allocate points across your class’ three distinct talent trees, helping you shape your playstyle as you level and progress into endgame content.

From this menu, you can spend talent points to unlock powerful passive effects and abilities that support your chosen specialization. 

It also allows you to save and manage multiple talent specializations, making it easy to switch between different builds at any time. You can link your Mystic Enchanting Specialization and Equipment Sets to your build so that your gear and enchants update automatically when you swap. 

Additionally, the menu displays all your class-specific spells in one organized place, helping you track what you’ve learned and plan future upgrades.

The Call Board is a useful quest hub found near the entrances of every Capital City, designed to help players stay on track throughout their journey.

While leveling, the Call Board directs you to the next appropriate questing area, ensuring smooth zone progression and helping you avoid out-leveling content. It’s especially handy for new players or those unsure of where to go next.

At the maximum level, the Call Board offers daily and weekly quests that provide a variety of rewards, including Marks of Ascension, valuable Currency, rare or epic equipment, and more. These quests often encourage players to revisit dungeons, complete world events, or engage in other content that contributes to their overall progression.

For added convenience, you can acquire a portable call board, which lets you access these quests from anywhere in the world. You can buy a call board for your faction or a neutral one that can be used by all characters from the Auction House or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

While leveling, the Call Board guides you to the next questing zone to continue your journey. At max level, it offers daily and weekly quests with valuable rewards. \r\n\r\nYou can find the Call Board near the entrance of your Capital City.

Capital cities are the main social and logistical hubs for players of each faction. These cities serve as vital gathering points where players can access essential services such as the Bank for storing and retrieving items, the Auction House to buy and sell goods with other players, and the Call Board for picking up quests and coordinating group activities.

For the Alliance, Stormwind stands as the grand capital city, an enormous medieval-style kingdom filled with vendors, trainers, guild halls, and iconic landmarks. Meanwhile, the Horde’s capital is Orgrimmar, a fortified city built into the harsh landscapes of Durotar, reflecting the faction’s rugged and tribal culture.

Once players reach level 20, they receive a valuable convenience item called the Scroll of Retreat. This item is automatically added to their Vanity Collection and allows them to instantly teleport back to their faction’s capital city, making travel and access to services much easier, especially after completing quests or dungeons far from home.

Capital cities also act as social hubs where players can meet, trade, form groups, and participate in various in-game events.

The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is where you define and develop your build. Every class in CoA features multiple specializations, each with its own talent tree and unique class tree, offering a deep and customizable path for character progression.

From this menu, you can select or switch your Specialization, choosing between distinct playstyles within your class. 

You’ll spend points in your class tree to unlock signature abilities and defining mechanics, and invest in your talent tree to boost core stats, survivability, or damage potential. 

The menu also lets you import builds from the community or create your own to share. You can save multiple specializations and freely swap between them, making it easy to shift roles or strategies as needed.

The Character Info panel (Hotkey C) is your central hub for managing your character’s gear, stats, and key progression details.

It shows all currently equipped items and provides a full breakdown of combat stats like Strength, Intellect, Spell Power, Critical Strike chance, and more. Hovering over any stat or item reveals a tooltip with detailed explanations and comparisons.

From this menu, you can also access the equipment manager to save and assign equipment sets or choose a cosmetic title from those you've unlocked.

Class trainers are NPCs that specialize in a single class and allow you to learn new abilities and higher ranks of spells you’ve acquired. 

You will only be able to train at your corresponding class trainer. These trainers teach you all the abilities and upgrades available to your chosen class as you level.

You can locate class trainers by speaking to a guard in any Capital City or by using the Map Lens on your mini-map to highlight nearby trainers. They're typically found in class-specific training halls or districts.

For added convenience, players can use the Book of Ascension regardless if it's their own companion or another player’s. This all-in-one tool functions as a universal class trainer, allowing you to learn any available spells or ranks without needing to travel.

Class trainers specialize in one class and can teach you new spells as well as higher ranks of existing spells. \r\n\r\nTo find a class trainer, use the Map Lens to locate one on your mini-map or ask a guard in a Capital City.

Cogsworth is an NPC vendor located near Millhouse Manastorm at the entrance of your Capital City. He plays an important role in the Manastorm system, offering a variety of Manastorm Spells and upgrade items in exchange for Bonzo Bolts which is a Currency earned by progressing through the Manastorm.\r\n\r\nThe items Cogsworth sells are designed to enhance your effectiveness in the Manastorm, from powerful spells that help in tougher encounters to useful upgrades that provide more control, survivability, or utility as you climb.

Cooking is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession, focused on preparing food that grants temporary buffs, restores health, and improves combat effectiveness. Cooks create a wide variety of consumables that can boost Primary Attributes and secondary stats.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn cooking. Once trained, you can start collecting the ingredients required for your Recipes. Cooking materials are primarily gathered from beasts in the open world, caught through Fishing, or purchased from Vendors.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes that teach you how to prepare specific meals and feasts to share with your friends. Higher-level meals often grant stronger and more specialized buffs, making them highly sought after for Raid preparation or competitive gameplay.

Cooking does not require any special tool to craft, however, players often pair cooking with Fishing to maintain a steady supply of materials.

Companions are small, non-combat pets that accompany your character alongside your Tamed Pet. While they don’t participate in battles, many companions provide useful services that enhance your gameplay experience.

Treasure Keeper - Serves as a portable Bank.
Book of Ascension - Serves as a portable Class Trainer.

Courier Malik is an NPC located inside the Auction Houses of your Capital City. He facilitates the transfer of unbound vanity items (such as mounts, pets, toys, and other cosmetics) between the Seasonal Realm and Area: 52 servers.

Only non-consumable vanity items that can be saved in your Vanity Collection are eligible for transfer through Courier Malik. Consumable items cannot be sent this way. When items are transferred, they become instantly bound to your Vanity Collection on the receiving server and cannot be traded, mailed, or sold, ensuring your cosmetic collection remains personal and secure.

The transfer process is simple and free, making it an essential tool for maintaining and unifying your Vanity Collection across different realms.

Courier Malik, found in city Auction Houses, allows players to send unbound vanity items (those stored in the Vanity Collection) between the Seasonal Server and Area: 52. \r\n\r\nItems sent this way become instantly bound to your Vanity Collection and cannot be traded.

A Craftsman’s Codex is a consumable item that unlocks an additional Primary Profession slot for the character it is used on. This allows you to learn and level a third Primary Profession, expanding your crafting and gathering capabilities beyond the usual two-slot limit.

You can use multiple codexes on a single character (one for each additional profession slot) until you have unlocked every Primary Profession. This gives you the freedom to master every crafting and gathering trade if you wish.

You can purchase a codex off of the Auction House, from Tiraxis or from Nozdormu for in-game Currency, or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Critical Strike damage bonus is a stat that boosts the percentage damage dealt when you land a Critical Strike, making your critical hits even more powerful. This bonus can be increased through various Talents and abilities.

However, these base values can be enhanced by increasing your damage bonus.

DPS (Damage Per Second) functions both as a player’s role, and as a unit of measurement reported by addons to determine the damage output of a player or group.

A DPS player specializes in dealing damage to enemies, aiming to reduce their health as quickly and efficiently as possible.

DPS players focus on using a variety of offensive abilities, spells, and weapon attacks to maximize their damage output while managing resources like mana, energy, or rage. They often rely on positioning, timing, and crowd control to enhance their effectiveness.

Draft Mode adds a unique twist to character progression by letting you choose one ability from three random, classless options every other level. This system introduces an element of luck and creativity, encouraging you to experiment with different playstyles and combinations.

While your abilities are chosen through Draft Mode, your Talents remain fully customizable, allowing you to personalize your character’s power and strategy.

Once you reach max level, you can refine your chosen abilities using Hands of Fate, a special item purchased with Marks of Ascension. Hands of Fate let you redraw your abilities, giving you the freedom to fine-tune your build and craft the perfect setup for your playstyle.

Draft Mode lets you choose one ability from three random, classless options every other level, adding variety to your build while keeping Talents customizable. \r\n\r\nAt max level, you can use Hands of Fate (purchased with Marks of Ascension) to redraw and optimize your abilities.

The Dungeon Finder is a convenient tool that quickly connects you with other players to run dungeons together. To use it, open the Dungeons and Raids menu (Hotkey i), select your preferred role (Tank, Healer, or DPS) and choose whether to queue for a specific dungeon or a random dungeon (often called Random Dungeon Finder or RDF).

Once the system finds a group, you’ll be instantly teleported to the Dungeon, where you can earn Experience, gear, and complete quests. After finishing your run, simply right-click the Dungeon finder icon on your minimap and select “Leave Dungeon” to return to the open world.

Choosing to run random dungeons or filling a role that’s in high demand often grants bonus loot and rewards, making the Dungeon Finder one of the fastest and most popular ways to level up and prepare for endgame content.

The Dungeon Finder (Hotkey i) quickly matches you with other players for Dungeon runs based on your chosen role and Dungeon preference, teleporting you directly inside to earn Experience, gear, and rewards. \r\n\r\nBonuses are often granted for random dungeons or in-demand roles, making it a fast and popular way to level and prepare for endgame content.

Dungeons are five-player instanced challenges with elite enemies, tough bosses, and valuable loot, essential for leveling and endgame progression as they scale with your strength. 

You can access them through entrances across the open world or with the Dungeon Finder (RDF), which matches you with a group and teleports you inside. More difficult dungeons aren’t available through RDF due to difficulty, requiring you to manually form a Party (often via World Chat) and travel to the entrance. There are four types of dungeons:

Normal Dungeon – Available while leveling or shortly after reaching max level. A good place to learn boss mechanics and earn baseline gear.

Heroic Dungeon – Tougher versions designed for max-level characters. Enemies hit harder, and bosses drop better loot, including Marks of Triumph or Badges of Justice.

Mythic Dungeon – Even more challenging, with stronger mobs and enhanced mechanics. Mythic dungeons are typically run with organized groups aiming for high performance and better loot.

Mythic+ – A competitive, timed version of Mythic dungeons that scales in difficulty with each level. Completing these challenges rewards powerful gear and seasonal rewards.

Dungeons are five-player instanced challenges featuring elite mobs, tough bosses, and valuable loot. 

You can either find their entrances in the open world or use the Dungeon Finder to join a group instantly.

Durability is a system that tracks how much wear and tear your equipment takes during gameplay.  Weapons and armor have a durability value that gradually decreases as you engage in combat. Taking damage, using abilities, and especially dying all contribute to durability loss.

When a piece of gear reaches zero durability, it breaks. Broken items lose all of their stat bonuses, armor value, and effects, making them completely unusable until repaired.

To restore durability, visit any repair Vendor, typically found in towns, quest hubs, and capital cities. These NPCs can be quickly located using the Map Lens by searching for 'Repair.' Repairing gear costs gold, with more powerful items generally requiring more to fix.

Keeping your gear in good condition is vital, especially before entering dungeons, battlegrounds, or high-risk zones. Don’t wait until something breaks mid-fight, repair early and often.
Equipment durability decreases during combat and death, and when it reaches zero, your gear becomes broken and unusable and must be fixed at a repair NPC who can be located using the Map Lens.

Donation items are special items obtained through the Ascension Store, typically purchased using Donation Points (DP). These items are designed to provide convenience, cosmetic customization, and utility, without offering unfair power advantages in competitive content.

While most donation items are acquired through the online store, many can also be found on the Auction House, allowing players to purchase them with in-game currency instead of Donation Points. This makes them accessible to all players, whether or not they spend real money.

Most donation items fall into one of two categories:

Consumables – Useful tools like a Craftsman’s Codex, an Experience booster, or Tomes of Specialization.

Vanity Collection Items – Mounts, toys, cosmetic equipment, Companions, Heirlooms, and other Realm-Bound unlocks are stored safely in your Vanity Collection, where they can be accessed by any character on the same server.

Donation items are items obtained from the Ascension Store. These items can be bought from the online shop for Donation Points or found from the Auction House for in-game currency. \r\n\r\nMost donation items are either consumables, or can be found saved within your Vanity Collection.

Once stored, that enchant becomes available to any character you play on the realm, perfect for sharing powerful enchants across multiple builds and alternative characters.

While you can view and manage your collection anywhere, applying enchants to your Active Enchant Slots from your collection still requires a visit to an Enchanting Altar and requires Mystic Orbs.

Upon entering the Manastorm, every player is granted an Endless Manastorm Potion, a reusable consumable with a short cooldown that restores your health, energy, mana, and rage. This versatile potion is placed directly into your inventory and is designed to help you sustain yourself during the relentless encounters inside the Manastorm.

The potion’s effectiveness scales with group size, providing the most healing when you’re running solo, and slightly less when in larger parties. This scaling ensures it remains balanced and useful whether you’re tackling the Manastorm alone or with a full raid group.

Because the Manastorm can be punishing, keeping this potion handy on your action bar is essential for survival, allowing you to quickly recover and push deeper into the dungeon’s challenges.

Upon entering the Manastorm, each player receives an Endless Manastorm Potion, a reusable, short-cooldown item that restores health, energy, mana, and rage. \r\n\r\nIts effectiveness scales with group size, offering the most healing when solo.

Engineering is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession for players who want to invent powerful gadgets, explosives, and utility items that can enhance the way you play. Engineers craft unique tools, devices, and trinkets that offer both combat advantages and quirky mechanical effects.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn engineering. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the materials needed. Engineering relies heavily on metal bars and stone gathered and smelted through Mining, though many Recipes also require components sourced by Vendors, enemy loot, or parts crafted through another Profession.

As you level up, you'll unlock Recipes, known as schematics, that teach you how to craft many items that can’t be found through other professions, like teleporters, parachutes, and combat-enhancing bombs.

Crafting engineering items requires an rclight spanner, a tool that must remain in your inventory to make most schematics. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

Engineering is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that invents powerful gadgets, explosives, and utility items that enhance the way you play.\r\n\r\nEngineering is reliant on Mining for materials.

Epic enchants are powerful mystic enchants that you can equip in up to three Active Enchant Slots simultaneously. These enchants provide significant boosts to your character’s stats and abilities, often unlocking new spells, passive effects, or unique mechanics that can change how your character plays.\r\n\r\nBecause of their power, an epic Mystic Enchant is highly sought after by players aiming to optimize their builds or explore new playstyles. Equipping the right combination of epic enchants can elevate your effectiveness in PvE, PvP, or solo content.
Players can have three epic quality enchants applied in their Active Enchant Slots at a time. These enchants offer huge power boosts, new spells, and can unlock entirely new ways to play.

The Ethereal Bazaar is a special, ever-changing shop accessible through Tiraxis inside the Auction House of any Capital City. Unlike regular Vendors, the bazaar offers a selection of rare and exclusive cosmetic items that you won’t find anywhere else.

To purchase from the Ethereal Bazaar, you’ll need Bazaar Tokens, an item purchased from the Auction House or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP). 

Keep in mind that the bazaar’s inventory rotates on a random timer, and only one copy of each item is available per cycle. This means you’ll often compete with other players to snag these limited items before they disappear.

The Ethereal Bazaar is a unique shop accessible through Tiraxis inside the Auction House of any Capital City. \r\n\r\nIt offers rare and exclusive cosmetics in exchange for Bazaar Tokens but the selection rotates on a random timer and only one copy of each item is available per cycle.

Experience (also known as XP or EXP) is the core system that tracks your character’s progress toward the next level until the maximum level is achieved. The maximum level is 60 for Vanilla, 70 for the Burning Crusade Expansion, and 80 for Wrath of the Lich King.

You gain experience by doing a wide variety of activities in the world, including:

Completing Quests
Defeating Enemies
Exploring a New Sub-Zone
Gathering or Crafting using a Profession
Participating in Battlegrounds or World Events

Your experience bar is located along the bottom of the screen, showing your progress toward the next level. Once the bar is filled, your character levels up and grants new stat points, spell options, Talents and more.

Your experience gain can be boosted by items like Heirlooms, Rested Experience from an Inn, and Hotspots, which offer bonus experience in specific zones.

You can gain experience (or XP) by completing a quest, exploring a new sub-zone, gathering or crafting with a Profession, and defeating an enemy. \r\n\r\nYour experience bar is located at the bottom of the screen - fill it to reach the next level.

Expertise is a secondary stat that reduces the chance your attacks will be dodged or parried by enemies. This means your attacks are more likely to land successfully, improving your overall damage and combat effectiveness.\r\n\r\nYou can find your current expertise in Character Info (Hotkey C).
Expertise is a secondary stat that reduces the chance that your attacks will be dodged or parried.

Equipment Sets let you quickly swap between different gear loadouts using the equipment manager (Hotkey C -> Equipment Manager Tab) a built-in tool designed to make changing builds fast and efficient. 

The equipment manager allows you to save your current gear as a named set, making it easy to switch between setups. When you activate a saved set, the system will automatically equip the correct items whether they’re in your inventory or stored in your bank.

You can also assign specific equipment sets to your Specialization, so your gear automatically swaps to match the build you're using.

You can save gear loadouts using the Equipment Manager (Hotkey C -> Equipment Manager Tab). \r\n\r\nSwitching sets will automatically equip the appropriate items from your inventory or bank, making it easy to swap builds on the fly.

Fel Commutation is a special gear protection system used in High-Risk PvP Mode, allowing players to safeguard up to three specific pieces of equipment from being dropped when they die. It acts like a form of insurance, helping reduce the sting of PvP losses without fully removing the risk.

When you commutate, you select which three gear pieces (such as weapons, trinkets, or armor) you want to protect. If you die while flagged for high-risk, these protected items will be immune to loot drops, ensuring you keep your most valuable gear. However, a small gold fee will be automatically deducted each time fel commutation activates upon death.

You can access the Fel Commutation Portal in any Capital City by looking for its icon on the World Map or asking a guard. It’s a vital system for players diving into dangerous PvP zones, especially those carrying valuable equipment or farming high-stakes objectives.

Fel Commutation is a form of insurance for High-Risk PvP, letting you protect up to three specific pieces of gear from being dropped on death. \r\n\r\nA small gold fee is charged each time you die while protected.

A Feather of the Ancients is a convenience item that instantly unlocks every Flightpath for your character within a specific expansion. It’s an invaluable tool for players who want to skip the slow process of manually discovering each Flightmaster, especially on alts or during seasonal leveling.

There are different versions of the feather for each expansion:

Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms – Unlocks all Vanilla (Classic) flightpaths.
Outland – Unlocks all The Burning Crusade flightpaths.
Northrend – Unlocks all Wrath of the Lich King flightpaths.

Once obtained, feathers are stored in your Vanity Collection and can be used account-wide on any character.

You can acquire Feathers of the Ancients from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, as well as the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Using a Feather of the Ancients instantly unlocks all Flightpaths for your character. \r\n\r\nFeathers are stored in your Vanity Collection and can be obtained from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, as well as the Ascension Store for Donation Points.

Fishing is a Secondary Skill and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Fish gathered through this skill are used in a Crafting Profession like Alchemy or Cooking.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn fishing. Once trained, you can begin gathering fish, or even buried treasure, by locating the nearest body of water. Once leveling to fishing skill 100, you can use a Weather-Beaten Journal that will teach you the skill to 'Find Fish' using the Map Lens. This highlights nearby pools with schools of fish where you have a much higher chance to get specific items.

Each time you collect an item from the water, you have a chance to contribute to your Fishing skill and provide fish-based materials used directly in crafting. Different zones contain different types of fish, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

To catch fish, you’ll need a Fishing Rod, which must be equipped and can be purchased from Vendors. You can also enhance your fishing ability by attaching lures to your rod. These can also be bought from Vendors, and will temporarily boost your fishing skill allowing you to fish in higher-level waters.

Fishing is a Secondary Skill and a Gathering Profession that allows you to gather fish and other items from bodies of water throughout the world.\r\n\r\nThe materials you catch are used in the Crafting Profession Cooking and occasionally Alchemy.

First Aid is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession, focused on creating bandages and other medical supplies that restore health quickly in and out of combat.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn first aid. Once trained, you can start collecting the necessary materials, which primarily consists of cloth dropped by humanoid enemies in the open world. These materials are then processed into bandages of increasing potency as you level up this skill.

As you progress, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as manuals, that teach you how to craft stronger bandages and other healing items.

First aid does not require any tools or special crafting locations, making it one of the most accessible and low-maintenance skills to use.

First aid is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession that lets you craft bandages, which restore health over time and can be used during combat.\r\n\r\nFirst aid uses cloth dropped from humanoid enemies for materials.

Flightpaths (FP) are a fast-travel system, allowing players to quickly fly between specific, connected locations across the open world. They’re essential for cutting down travel time, especially when questing or moving between distant zones.

To use a flightpath, you must first unlock its node by speaking to the local Flightmaster. You can also instantly unlock certain nodes by using special items like the Feather of the Ancients, which reveals multiple locations at once.

However, you can only fly between nodes that are directly connected and already discovered. If you're trying to travel across multiple zones, you’ll need to have unlocked all the Flightmasters along the route, otherwise, the system won’t allow you to fly to your intended destination.

Once enough nodes are unlocked, you can chain multiple points together to create efficient travel routes, making it much easier to return to old quest hubs, dungeons, or cities.

Flightpaths are accessed through any Flightmaster, typically marked with a wing icon on your World Map and mini-map. When planning your journey, be sure to use the Map Lens to find nearby Flightmasters and keep your travel network growing.

Flightpaths (FP) are a fast-travel system that lets you fly between specific locations. \r\n\r\nTo use a flightpath, you must first unlock its node by speaking to the local Flightmaster or by using a Feather of the Ancients.

A flightmaster is an NPC that provides fast travel between different zones and towns across the world using a Flightpath. Speaking to a flightmaster for the first time unlocks their location, allowing you to travel back there later from other connected flightmasters.

Undiscovered flightmasters are marked with a green (!) above their heads, making them easy to spot as you explore new areas. Once unlocked, they will appear as wing icons on your World Map, showing all the places your character can fly to from any given location.

You can also use the Map Lens to highlight nearby flightmasters, helping you quickly locate the nearest point of fast travel.
Speaking to a flightmaster unlocks their Flightpath for future use. \r\n\r\nUndiscovered flightmasters are marked with a green (!) above their heads.

Ascension’s seasonal realms are time-limited servers designed to offer a fresh start, unique challenges, and a competitive environment for players looking to play the game in new and exciting ways. Each season typically introduces a special game mode, such as Draft Mode, Wildcard Mode, or Felforged, encouraging players to experiment with different builds and strategies.

Progression on seasonal servers usually begins in Vanilla WoW content and gradually unlocks expansions and new systems, eventually culminating in the current patch found on Area: 52, Ascension’s permanent progression realm. This seasonal structure creates a focused, level playing field where players race for Server Firsts, dominate leaderboards, and chase exclusive cosmetic and vanity rewards.

At the end of the season, the realm is closed and characters are transferred to Area: 52, bringing their gear, titles, and seasonal rewards with them. This ensures your progress is preserved, while keeping the core seasonal journey competitive and time-bound.

Ascension’s seasonal realms are time-limited servers that reset at the end of each season. \r\n\r\nThey often feature unique game modes and progression that begins in Vanilla content and advances through to the current patch on Area: 52.

Gathering professions are a category of Primary Profession that allows players to gather raw materials from the world to supply various a Crafting Profession.

The available gathering professions are:

Herbalism - Gather herbs used in Alchemy and other crafting recipes.
Mining - Extract ore and stone from mineral nodes, used in Blacksmithing and Engineering.
Skinning - Collect leather, hides, and scales from slain beasts, used in Leatherworking.
Woodcutting - Chop down trees to turn into lumber and turn in for quests.

Gathering professions are a great way to earn gold, supply yourself or your Guild with necessary crafting materials, and engage more deeply with the world’s diverse zones.
Gathering professions involve exploring the world to collect resources from nodes or defeated enemies. \r\n\r\nThese materials are essential to level a Crafting Profession.

Guilds are player-created communities that bring adventurers together under a shared banner. Whether you’re looking for friends to chat with, teammates for Dungeons and Raids, or just a sense of belonging in the world, joining a guild opens the door to more social and rewarding gameplay.

Being part of a guild gives you access to several valuable features, including a guild chat channel as well as a Guild Bank to collect and share items with your guildmates.

To find a guild, keep an eye on the global chat for recruitment messages or check your realm’s Discord server, where many guilds advertise their goals and playstyles.

If you’d rather lead than join, you can start your own guild by visiting your faction’s Guild Master NPC, found in major cities. For a small fee, you can purchase a Guild Charter, gather a few signatures from fellow players, and form your own community from scratch.

Guilds are player-created communities that provide social connection, facilitate group content opportunities, and exclusive perks. \r\n\r\nJoining a guild lets you interact with other players and share a Guild Bank with your teammates.

Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that increases your attack speed, casting speed, and energy regeneration. This allows you to use your abilities more rapidly, improving your overall damage output and responsiveness in combat.\r\n\r\nYou can find your current haste rating in the Character Info (Hotkey C).
Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that boosts your attack speed, casting speed, and energy regeneration, letting you unleash abilities more rapidly.

Hardcore Trials are special challenge modes that reward players for reaching the maximum level without dying. Designed to test your skill, focus, and knowledge of the game, these Trials offer unique rewards and bragging rights to those who survive the journey from level 1 to maximum without falling in battle.

To begin a hardcore trial, your character must be level 1. Visit Stony Tark, found in your starting zone or Capital City, to activate the trial. It's important to note that you must start the trial before gaining any Experience. Additionally, you won’t be able to trade, use the mailbox, or access the Auction House until after you’ve started the challenge.

During the trial, if your character dies even once, the challenge is failed. However, unlike perma-death modes, your character will revive normally and can continue to play the game as usual, they simply won’t receive the tardcore trial rewards.

Successfully completing a hardcore trial often grants you cosmetics, titles, vanity items, or other exclusive rewards, making it a popular option for players seeking thrilling and rewarding gameplay.

Hardcore Trials are challenging game modes that reward players for reaching the maximum level without dying. \r\n\r\nIf you die during the trial, you fail the challenge, but your character can still revive and continue playing as normal.

Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that increases your physical attack and spell casting speed. This allows you to use your abilities more rapidly, improving your overall damage output and responsiveness in combat.\r\n\r\nYou can find your current haste rating in the Character Info (Hotkey C).
Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that boosts your attack and casting speed, letting you unleash abilities more rapidly.

A Healer is a player who specializes in restoring health and keeping their group alive during combat.

Healers use a variety of healing spells, buffs, and protective abilities to mend damage taken by teammates and prevent deaths. They must carefully manage their resources and prioritize targets to ensure the group stays alive through challenging encounters. 

In addition to direct healing, Healers often provide utility through removing harmful effects, dispelling debuffs, and offering supportive buffs that enhance the group’s survivability.

A Healer specializes in mending damage and keeping their group alive during combat. \r\n\r\nUsing healing spells, buffs, and protective abilities, healers ensure their teammates survival and are essential in both PvP and PvE content.

Healing power is a secondary stat that increases the effectiveness of your healing spells and abilities. The higher your Healing Power, the more health your abilities restore, making it essential for all healing-focused builds.\r\n\r\nYou can view your healing power in Character Info (Hotkey C).
Healing power is a secondary stat that increases the effectiveness of your healing spells and abilities.

A Hearthstone is an item that allows your character to instantly teleport back to the Inn you've set as your current home location. Every player starts with a Hearthstone automatically, bound to their starter zone, and it can be used to quickly return to town for safety, repairs, or quest turn-ins. You can change your home location by speaking with any Innkeeper and selecting the 'Make this Inn your home.' option.

If your Hearthstone is ever lost or deleted, it can be easily replaced by talking to any innkeeper, who will provide a new one at no cost. Hearthstones have a 30 minute cooldown, so they’re best used strategically when fast travel is needed.

In addition to travel, Hearthstones also have a unique purpose as they serve as an all-in-one totem reagent. Totem-based abilities depend on having a hearthstone in your inventory, so it’s important to keep one with you at all times, even if you use alternate travel methods like teleport scrolls or portals.

A Hearthstone lets you teleport to your set Inn location and is essential for quick travel, safety, and totem-based abilities. \r\n\r\nIt has a 30-minute cooldown, can be replaced for free at any innkeeper, and should always be kept in your inventory.

Heirlooms are special pieces of Realm-Bound gear designed to scale with your character as they level, making them ideal for leveling alternative characters or speeding up the journey to maximum level. These items not only increase in power as your character gains levels, but many also provide bonus Experience, helping you level faster through quests, kills, and battlegrounds.

Heirlooms are stored in your Vanity Collection and are accessible to all characters on the same realm. Once unlocked, you can equip heirlooms on any eligible character, giving you a powerful head start with solid stats and consistent performance across all level ranges.

Most heirlooms come in the form of weapons, armor, and trinkets, and some are themed to match specific class roles, such as Strength-based melee, Intellect-based casters, or Agility-based archers.

Heirlooms can be obtained through various means, including purchasing them from Vendors for PvP Points, Prestige Points, Marks of Ascension, and from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).
Heirlooms are Realm-Bound gear that scales in power as you level and provides bonus Experience. \r\n\r\nStored in your Vanity Collection, they’re accessible to all your characters on the same realm.

Heirlooms are special pieces of Realm-Bound gear designed to scale with your character as they level, making them ideal for leveling alternative characters or speeding up the journey to maximum level. These items not only increase in power as your character gains levels, but many also provide bonus Experience, helping you level faster through quests, kills, and battlegrounds.

Heirlooms are stored in your Vanity Collection and are accessible to all characters on the same realm. However, characters must have prestiged at least once before they are eligible to equip heirlooms. Once that requirement is met, you can freely use heirlooms on any qualifying character, giving you a powerful head start with solid stats and consistent performance across all level ranges.

Most heirlooms come in the form of weapons, armor, and trinkets, and some are themed to match specific class roles, such as Strength-based melee, Intellect-based casters, or Agility-based archers.

Heirlooms can be obtained through various means, including purchasing them from Vendors for PvP Points, Prestige Points, Marks of Ascension, and from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Heirlooms are Realm-Bound gear that scales in power as you level and grants bonus Experience. They become accessible once your character reaches Prestige level 1 or higher. \r\n\r\nStored in your Vanity Collection, Heirlooms can be used by all your characters on the same realm.

Herbalism is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Herbs gathered by herbalists are used in Crafting Professions like Alchemy.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn herbalism. Once trained, you can begin gathering herbs by locating plant nodes found throughout the open world. After learning the Profession, you'll also unlock the 'Find Herbs' function in the Map Lens, which highlights nearby herb nodes, making it much easier to spot gathering opportunities as you explore.

Each herb node you gather has a chance to contribute to your herbalism skill and provides plant-based materials used directly in crafting. Different zones contain different types of herbs, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

While herbalism does not require a special tool to gather herbs, many players combine it with Crafting Professions like Alchemy to streamline their material supply. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

Herbalism is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession that gathers various plants from the environment.\r\n\r\nItems gathered from Herbalism are primarily used in the Crafting Profession Alchemy.

The Hero Architect (Hotkey N -> Hero Architect Tab) is a library of featured builds and community created builds that contain full loadouts of spells, Talents, recommended playstyles, macros, equipment suggestions, and various buff recommendations. \r\n\r\nYou can use it to discover new archetypes or share your setup with other players. Community builds can be created by anyone, but you can guarantee a powerful build with the 'Featured Builds' category, designed to teach you how to play effectively.

The Hero Architect (Hotkey N -> Hero Architect Tab) is a library of featured builds and community created builds. You can use it to discover new archetypes or share your setup with other players. \r\n\r\nFeatured builds guarantee a powerful build designed to teach you how to play it effectively.

Heroic dungeons are tougher, maximum level versions of regular dungeons, designed to offer greater challenges and significantly improved rewards. These dungeons feature enhanced enemies, harder-hitting bosses, and more complex mechanics, making them a key part of any player’s endgame progression.

To enter a heroic Dungeon from the open world, right-click your character portrait, select 'Dungeon Difficulty', and switch to 'Heroic' before entering the instance. Otherwise simply select the Dungeon you desire from the specific list, or use the 'Random Heroic Dungeon' option from the Dungeon Finder.

Heroic dungeons offer access to endgame PvE currencies. Bosses in these dungeons drop either Marks of Triumph (in Vanilla content) or Badges of Justice (in Burning Crusade content).

These currencies can be exchanged at special vendors in your Capital City or PvE hub for specific pieces of Dungeon-quality gear, giving players a guaranteed path to upgrades even if the boss doesn’t drop what they need directly. This system helps ensure that everyone in the group can make progress.

Heroic dungeons are a core stepping stone into the next Raid, mythic Dungeon, and high-end character builds, offering a reliable way to gear up and master your role.
Heroic dungeons are tougher versions of normal dungeons, designed for maximum level characters. \r\n\r\nExpect stronger enemies, more powerful bosses, and significantly better loot.

High-Risk PvP Mode is a ruleset designed for players seeking a high-stakes, full-loot PvP extravaganza. 

In this mode, defeating other players allows you to loot their gear and inventory, creating intense and rewarding encounters. However, the danger goes both ways, if you die, you risk dropping a piece of your equipped gear, along with items from your bags.

To help manage the risk, players can use Fel Commutation, a system that allows you to protect specific gear pieces from being dropped on death. 

Items that are not protected by Fel Commutation and are looted in High-Risk PvP Mode immediately become Bloodforged with powerful PvP stats.

To enable High-Risk mode, head to your Capital City and open the Hybrid Risk menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab), then select 'High-Risk PvP Mode' as your active ruleset. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.

This is a ruleset that allows players to engage in open-world PvP and loot gear and items from defeated opponents but risk losing their own if they die. \r\n\r\nEquipment can be protected using Fel Commutation for a price, and looted items become powerful Bloodforged gear.

The Hit Cap refers to the minimum amount of Hit Rating a player needs to never miss an attack on an enemy. Reaching the hit cap ensures your offensive abilities connect reliably, especially in high level content like Dungeons and Raids.

The hit cap is divided into two categories, players and Raid bosses.

To never miss a player with a physical attack or spell, you need 4% Hit Rating.
To never miss a Raid boss with a physical attack, you need 8% Hit Rating.
To never miss a Raid boss with a spell, you need 17% Hit Rating. 

Raid bosses have higher resistance and avoidance, meaning players typically need a higher Hit Cap to perform consistently in endgame content.

If you're at or above the hit cap, any extra Hit Rating provides no additional benefit and could be better spent on other stats like Critical Strike or Haste.

You can find your hit cap by mousing over “Hit Rating” in Character Info (Hotkey C).
The Hit Cap is the minimum Hit Rating needed to ensure your attacks never miss (4% for players, 8% for Raid bosses with physical attacks, and 17% for Raid bosses with spells).

Hit rating is a secondary stat that increases your chance to successfully land spells and abilities on your target. It helps prevent your attacks from missing, which is vital for maintaining a consistent damage output.

Melee, ranged, and spell attacks each have their own Hit Cap. Reaching the appropriate Hit Cap for your build and content type (PvE or PvP) is a key part of optimizing performance.

You can find your current hit rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).
Hit rating is a secondary stat that increases your chance to hit with spells and abilities. \r\n\r\nMelee, ranged, and spells require different amounts of hit to ensure you never miss a target.

A Hotspot is a temporary, rotating area in the open world that offers a bonus to Experience gained from defeating enemies and completing quests within its boundaries.

When a hotspot becomes active, it’s announced in the chat for players currently in that zone, making it easy to know when and where one has appeared. You can also identify a Hotspot by looking at your World Map (if you’re in the affected zone).

Hotspots rotate periodically and can appear in different zones, encouraging players to move around the world and take advantage of shifting leveling opportunities.

A Hotspot is a temporary area in the open world that grants bonus Experience for defeating enemies and completing quests. \r\n\r\nHotspots are announced within their zone when they appear, and you can also spot them on the World Map while you’re in that specific zone.

Honor Points are the main PvP Currency earned by participating in Player vs. Player activities. You can gain Honor by fighting in battlegrounds, engaging in open world PvP, completing PvP daily quests, and participating in PvP events. The more you contribute to defeating enemy players and completing objectives, the more Honor you’ll earn.

Your current total is stored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Honor Points can be spent at PvP Quartermasters, who offer a wide variety of PvP-focused rewards, including seasonal gear, weapons, Mounts, cosmetic items, and other useful tools for both combat and style.

Honor Points are gained through various PvP activities. \r\n\r\nStored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab), Honor Points can be used to purchase gear, mounts, and other items at a PvP Quartermaster.

A PvP Quartermaster is a vendor who sells rare and epic Quality PvP gear, available in exchange for Honor Points and Arena Points. These Vendors are your main source of PvP equipment outside of Bloodforged gear.

PvP Quartermasters are typically found in Capital Cities and PvP-focused hubs throughout the world. To locate them easily, look for the PvP icon on the World Map or ask a guard.

The gear sold by these quartermasters is seasonal, meaning it changes with each competitive PvP season to reflect updated balance and rewards.

PvP Quartermasters sell seasonal PvP gear for Honor Points and Arena Points. \r\n\r\nThese NPCs are located in Capital Cities or PvP hubs and can be found by asking a city guard or searching for the PvP icon on the World Map.

Ascension features a unique hybrid-risk PvP system that gives players full control over how they engage with enemy players in combat. Instead of locking everyone into a single PvP ruleset, you can choose from three distinct modes (PvE Mode, No-Risk PvP Mode, and High-Risk PvP Mode) each offering a different level of intensity, danger, and reward. 

This system ensures that players with different goals and playstyles can coexist in the same world while enjoying the game on their own terms.

PvE Mode and No-Risk PvP Mode players share the same game world, meaning both PvE and PvP players can interact with the environment and each other (within their ruleset boundaries) without being forced into unwanted combat.

To select your PvP ruleset, visit your Capital City and open the hybrid risk menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab), then choose the mode that best fits your current gameplay goals. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.
Ascension features a hybrid risk PvP system, letting players choose their preferred PvP ruleset. \r\n\r\nYou can opt for PvE Mode, No-Risk PvP Mode, or High-Risk PvP Mode depending on your playstyle.

Inns are important locations found in most quest hubs, towns, and cities throughout the world. Each inn is managed by an innkeeper, who can function as a vendor and bind your Hearthstone to their location.

To bind your Hearthstone, speak to the Innkeeper and select the option to 'Make this Inn your home.' Upon its next use, your Hearthstone will teleport you back to that location.

Inns also serve as rest areas, meaning if you log out inside an inn, you’ll gradually accumulate Rested Experience. Spending even a few hours offline in an inn can provide a significant Experience boost, making them valuable for both active and casual players.

To quickly find an inn or innkeeper in any area, use the Map Lens and select 'Innkeeper' to highlight any nearby Inns.
Most quest hubs and cities feature an inn, where players can find innkeepers to set their Hearthstone teleport location. \r\n\r\nLogging out inside an inn grants you Rested Experience.

Intellect is the Primary Attribute that represents mental acuity, magical knowledge, and the ability to harness arcane, divine, or elemental forces. It is a core stat for players who specialize in spellcasting, making it vital for dealing magic damage, healing allies, or using utility spells effectively.

Effects of intellect:

+1 Intellect increases your maximum Mana by 15.
+1 Intellect increases your Spell and Melee Critical Strike Rating.

Intellect also affects Mana Regeneration indirectly, especially when paired with Spirit or talents that scale from intellect.

Jewelcrafting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that is only available in Burning Crusade content and beyond.

Jewelcrafting focuses on cutting gems and crafting jewelry to enhance gear with powerful stat bonuses. Jewelcrafters can create rings, necklaces, trinkets, and cut gems used in sockets.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn jewelcrafting. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the necessary materials, primarily being raw gems and ores gathered through Mining.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as designs, that teach you how to cut specific gems and craft a variety of jewelry.

Creating most jewelcrafting items requires a jeweler’s kit, which must be in your inventory while crafting. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

Leatherworking is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession focused on turning hides and leathers gathered from beasts into a variety of practical items such as equipment and stat-boosting armor kits. Leatherworkers create essential gear for leather and mail wearers, as well as niche items that are required through specific endgame content.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn leatherworking. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the necessary materials. Leatherworking relies primarily on hides and leathers obtained by Skinning throughout the open world, which can then be processed into tougher materials used in crafting.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as patterns, that teach you how to craft specific armor pieces and useful gear enhancements. Leatherworkers can also create specialized items like armor kits that provide armor buffs, small Bags, toys, and unique gear that is required in various end-game content.

While Leatherworking does not need specific tools to craft, many players pair it with Skinning to streamline their material gathering. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

A legendary enchant is a powerful type of Mystic Enchant that serves as the centerpiece of most custom builds. Unlike rare or epic enchants, legendary enchants offer game-changing effects, often unlocking entirely new spells, mechanics, or class-defining abilities that can drastically enhance your character’s playstyle.

Players can equip one legendary enchant at a time in their Active Enchant Slots. Because of their power and uniqueness, choosing a legendary enchant is often the first step in crafting a build, as the rest of your enchants, Talents, and abilities are typically selected to support and enhance it.

Legendary enchants range from thematic class hybrids (like combining elemental magic with rogue techniques) to completely original effects, using new resource systems, or transforming spells into entirely new abilities. Many popular builds are centered around these enchants, making them a core part of character identity and progression.

Legendary enchants can be found through various means, including reforging Mystic Scrolls, discovering them as a Worldforged Mystic Enchant, or purchasing them off of the Auction House from other players.

Players can equip one legendary enchant in their Active Enchant Slots at a time. \r\n\r\nThese mystic enchants provide powerful, build-defining bonuses and unlock unique spells that open up entirely new playstyles!

LFG, short for 'Looking For Group', is a common term used by players who are seeking others to join them in multiplayer content such as Dungeons, Raids, world bosses, or group quests. If you're playing solo but want to take on group-based challenges, typing 'LFG' in chat (often followed by the name or level of the activity, like 'LFG 70 Dungeons' is the standard way to signal that you're available and ready to team up.\r\n\r\nThe opposite of this is LFM, or 'Looking For Member', which is used when a player or group already has a party started and is recruiting others to fill specific roles, such as a tank, healer, or DPS. For example, someone might post 'LFM Tank and Heals for mythic+' if they already have damage dealers and need the remaining roles.
Looking For Group, or LFG, is a common phrase used by solo players seeking a group of other people to join for Dungeons, Raids, or quests.
